explanation: Farmers bred them all from wild cabbage, Brassica oleracea, by favouring different parts: leaves for kale, flower heads for broccoli and cauliflower, side buds for sprouts.

claims.text: Broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower, kale and Brussels sprouts are all cultivated varieties of one species, Brassica oleracea.
These vegetables were bred from wild cabbage by selecting for different parts of the plant.
Kale was selected for its leaves, broccoli and cauliflower for their flower heads, and Brussels sprouts for their side buds.
